question: Which of these drugs is used as platelet antiaggregant, reversible antagonist of the P2Y12 receptor:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Ticagrelor -> reversible antagonist of the P2Y12 receptor -> platelet antiaggregant -> 95% CHAIN: Clopidogrel -> irreversible antagonist of the P2Y12 receptor -> platelet antiaggregant -> 90% CHAIN: Acetylsalicylic acid -> inhibits cyclooxygenase -> reduces thromboxane A2 production -> platelet antiaggregant (indirectly) -> 85% CHAIN: Tirofiban -> blocks the glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptor -> platelet antiaggregant -> 95%
enhanced_information: Ticagrelor is a reversible antagonist of the P2Y12 receptor, making it a platelet antiaggregant. Clopidogrel, on the other hand, is an irreversible antagonist of the P2Y12 receptor, also serving as a platelet antiaggregant. Acetylsalicylic acid indirectly acts as a platelet antiaggregant by inhibiting cyclooxygenase and reducing thromboxane A2 production. Tirofiban blocks the glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptor, leading to platelet antiaggregation. Therefore, the correct drug used as a platelet antiaggregant and reversible antagonist of the P2Y12 receptor is Ticagrelor.
analysis: Ticagrelor is a reversible antagonist of the P2Y12 receptor, making it a platelet antiaggregant. Clopidogrel, on the other hand, is an irreversible antagonist of the P2Y12 receptor. Given the specific requirement for a reversible antagonist of the P2Y12 receptor, Ticagrelor is the correct drug in this context.
